paras: The attempted lynching of Scott Garner took place in Anderson, South Carolina, on the night of about July 27, 1920, when a crowd gathered to seize a 14-year-old Black youth arrested on an accusation of attacking a white woman. Officers drew the crowd off with a decoy automobile while a deputy sheriff took Garner out of the city, reportedly toward Columbia. The episode survives in a single dispatch headlined "Probable Lynching Averted."

According to the Anderson dispatch, a "prominent young white woman" was standing in front of her home with her baby in her arms, waiting for her husband to return from putting his automobile in the garage, when she was seized. The dispatch said her attacker ran when she screamed and her husband came to her aid. Scott Garner, described as a "14-year-old colored youth," was later arrested at his home and taken before the woman, who with her husband identified him.

News of the affair spread over the city, and within a short time a crowd had gathered which, in the dispatch's words, "in all probability would have dealt severely" with Garner. Local officers answered with what the paper called "a clever ruse": as the crowd chased an automobile loaded with policemen, Deputy Sheriff Hilliard got away with the prisoner. Where Garner was taken was not announced, but it was thought the officers had headed for Columbia.
By the morning of July 28 Anderson was reported "quiet" after the night's excitement. No report of arrests among the crowd, of a trial of Garner, or of his later fate was found in the coverage.

The only report found ran on August 4 on page 7 of the Keowee Courier of Pickens Court House, an Anderson story dated July 28. Its headline, "Probable Lynching Averted," and deck, "Negro Attacked Anderson Woman—Officers Spirited Him Away," stated the accusation as fact, although the body said only that Garner "is alleged to have attacked" the woman. The story credited the officers' ingenuity, said nothing about the crowd beyond its likely intentions, and gave no account from Garner or his family.
No coverage of the episode was found in the Black press.

reader.title: Attempted lynching of Scott Garner
bases: A crowd gathered after the arrest of an accused Black youth and, by the report's own account, would 'in all probability' have dealt severely with him had officers not removed him by a ruse; the headline calls it a 'Probable Lynching Averted' (A1).
Only one report, a reprinted Anderson dispatch in the Keowee Courier, was found; no second paper or Black-press account appears in the coverage (A1).

accounts.label: Anderson dispatch (local/officers' account)
accounts.gist: Garner attacked the woman, was arrested and identified, and officers fooled the crowd with a decoy car so the deputy could take him away, probably to Columbia.

framing.detail: Headlined 'Probable Lynching Averted', it credits the officers' 'clever ruse' while presenting the accusation as largely settled ('Negro Attacked Anderson Woman') and the crowd's intent as a likely 'severe' reckoning, without comment on the mob.
